subject: Post-demo: vector-ranking POC scope, SDK hooks, and streaming fallback plan
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@quantv.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-17T09:05:00-05:00
Subject: Post-demo: vector-ranking POC scope, SDK hooks, and streaming fallback plan

Hi Liam / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side (calling out the two product goals you emphasized):

1) Improve search result relevance by re-ranking candidate documents using a lightweight vector ranking model (top-N rerank).
2) Reduce end-to-end latency for interactive search to <= 150ms for 95th percentile.

Key technical constraints you mentioned:
- Client uses a managed microservice (Java + Vert.x) for search, limited to 100ms compute budget per request for any additional network hop.
- Data residency: all query logs must remain in Region US-C (QuantV's AWS account).
- Budget target for POC: ~10k queries/day.

Proposed POC scope (attachment: QuantV-POC-scope-v1.pdf):
- Phase A (3 weeks): sample ingest (50k docs), embeddings via Redwood-hosted embedding model, host vector index in QuantV VPC (Private deployment), implement a sidecar rerank call.
- Phase B (2 weeks): swap to Redwood streaming rerank path with prefix caching for repeated queries, validate 95p latency.
- Deliverables: performance report, SDK hooks for Java sidecar, deployment runbook.

Two immediate asks for your team:
- Share a small sample dataset (anonymized) and a representative QPS profile by EOD next Tue (2026-11-24).
- Confirm whether QuantV legal will need a vendor security questionnaire up-front or after an architecture review.

Tech confirm items for our infra team (cc’d Aditya and Karthik):
- We plan to expose two integration options: (1) HTTP/JSON SDK hook (blocking call to Redwood rerank endpoint) and (2) streaming function-call style where the client streams tokens and gets a partial ranking score. Need to validate Java client constraints.
- Fallback plan: if streaming can't meet the 100ms compute hop requirement, we propose a hybrid: synchronous top-k coarse filter in-client + async finer rerank with cached top-1 replacement.

Attachments: QuantV-POC-scope-v1.pdf, redwood-sdk-hook-proposal.md

Next steps: can we lock a 45-minute technical sync with your infra and product engineers next Tue or Wed? I can send a calendar invite.

Best,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0183

[Attachment: redwood-sdk-hook-proposal.md (Markdown) — 1 page]

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@quantv.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@quantv.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T11:12:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: vector-ranking POC scope, SDK hooks, and streaming fallback plan

Thanks Naomi — appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We'll provide a 10k-row anonymized sample and QPS profile by 2026-11-24.
- Legal: we prefer the security questionnaire first (our SOC/compliance team wants to triage before infra access). Can you send Redwood's standard security questionnaire or link?
- For SDKs: our infra team strongly prefers an HTTP/JSON blocking call because adding streaming in Vert.x will be heavier on our side. However, if Redwood can demonstrate streaming with <100ms step latency, we may evaluate it for v2.

Also, two product-level acceptance criteria to add to the POC: 
1) Precision@10 uplift vs baseline of at least +8 percentage points on your eval set.
2) End-to-end 95p latency <= 150ms for interactive queries.

We can do the technical sync on Wed 2026-11-25 at 10:00 AM ET — I’ll invite our infra lead (Devon) and Priya (product).

Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Product, QuantV
liam.oconnor@quantv.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T08:17:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: vector-ranking POC scope, SDK hooks, and streaming fallback plan

Quick technical notes from runtime team: 

- Java blocking HTTP/JSON: easiest path. We'll provide a small Java SDK wrapper (blocking client + retry/backoff) and a JVM sidecar example. Expect initial patch in SDK repo by 2026-11-20.
- Streaming function-call: our streaming rerank API depends on low-overhead protobuf streams over gRPC or WebSocket. On-paper latency is good but requires client changes — Vert.x can do this but adds ~30-60ms overhead unless we do a native Netty path. That's why we recommend the hybrid route Naomi suggested.
- KV-prefix caching: to hit 95p target we recommend enabling prefix caching on queries with stable prefixes (we'll instrument sample traces during Phase A).
- Privacy/residency: For Private deployment inside QuantV VPC, we can run the embedding model inference in your VPC (model running on dedicated instances) so raw logs and embeddings never leave your account. Need account point-of-contact for infra onboarding and an IAM role for the onboarding playbook.

I'll draft the Java SDK stub and a short runbook for VPC onboarding. Assigning timeline: SDK stub by 2026-11-20, VPC runbook by 2026-11-22.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Lead Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Liam / Priya —

Thanks — this is great; we've updated the attached POC spec with your acceptance criteria (Precision@10 uplift +8pp, 95p latency <=150ms) and the legal ask. Action items and owners: 

1) QuantV: provide anonymized sample set + QPS profile by 2026-11-24 — Liam / Priya
2) QuantV: complete Redwood security questionnaire (link below) — Priya / Devon — target 2026-11-22
3) Redwood (Aditya): deliver Java SDK stub + sidecar example by 2026-11-20
4) Redwood (Aditya/Karthik): VPC onboarding runbook and IAM role template by 2026-11-22
5) Schedule tech sync Wed 2026-11-25 10:00 AM ET — calendar invite sent separately.

We will also generate a short eval harness (server-side) to measure Precision@10 uplift and latency under a replayed QPS. Aditya will include instructions for running the harness inside a customer VPC.

Links: Redwood security questionnaire — https://redwood.example.com/s/security-questionnaire; POC spec (updated) — https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cPOCSpec

If this looks right I’ll mark the POC kickoff as 2026-11-30 (allowing legal and infra to complete onboarding).

Best,
Naomi
